title: The American Revolution

cards.h: The Tea Party was about monopoly, not the price of tea
cards.b:
On 16 December 1773, men dressed as Mohawks boarded three ships in Boston harbour and dumped 342 chests of tea into the water. It looks like a story about a tax. It was really about a company.

The company was the East India Company, and it ties directly to us.

Britain won the Seven Years' War (1756-63) but was deep in debt. It taxed the American colonies: the Stamp Act (1765), then duties on tea, glass and paper.

Colonists said they had no representatives in Parliament, so taxes were unfair: 'no taxation without representation'. The Boston Massacre (1770) left five colonists dead.

The Tea Act (1773) actually made East India Company tea cheaper, even with the tax, but gave the Company a monopoly and accepted Parliament's right to tax. Merchants and radicals objected. Britain answered with harsh 'Coercive Acts' in 1774.

Fighting began in April 1775 at Lexington and Concord.

Thomas Jefferson drafted the Declaration, adopted on 4 July 1776 (the vote for independence was on 2 July). It said all men are created equal and have the right to life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness. Jefferson himself held enslaved people.

George Washington's Continental Army was often short of food and money. The big turn came when the Americans won at Saratoga in 1777, which convinced France to join them in 1778.

In 1781 a French fleet and army helped trap General Cornwallis at Yorktown. Britain recognised independence in the Treaty of Paris (1783).

The first system, the Articles of Confederation, was weak. A convention at Philadelphia wrote the Constitution in 1787, with separation of powers, a President and a Congress. The Bill of Rights followed (1791).

The revolution was a model for others, but it left slavery alone and gave voting rights to few.

Some say it was a political break, not a social upheaval, since the same rich men kept power. Others say the radical ideas of equality and republican government changed the world.

Myth check: 'Tea tax went up.' It did not; the price of legal tea was falling. The argument was about principle and about the Company's power.

The same company, the same general

Lord Cornwallis surrendered to Washington at Yorktown in October 1781. He did not end his career there. He became Governor-General of India in 1786 and fought Tipu Sultan in the Third Anglo-Mysore War, which ended in 1792 with half of Tipu's land lost. In 1793 he introduced the Permanent Settlement of Bengal.

The East India Company itself was part of the American story. The Tea Act of 1773, made to rescue the near-bankrupt Company, led to the Boston Tea Party in December that year. A failed empire in America and a growing one in India grew from the same trading corporation.

Five things to remember

  1. Taxes without representation sparked the crisis.
  2. The Tea Party (1773) was against a Company monopoly.
  3. Declaration of Independence was adopted on 4 July 1776.
  4. French help won Yorktown (1781).
  5. Cornwallis went on to India.

Think about it

  • Why did colonists fight over a small tax?
  • Can a revolution claim equality and keep slavery?
